profile.address: 616, 10th Street, Western Gateway, Des Moines, Polk County, Iowa, 50309
profile.reading:
Aureon operates a data center facility in downtown Des Moines, Iowa, at 616 10th Street in the city's Western Gateway district, according to the company's own published facility list, "Aureon's Connected Data Centers," and a corresponding listing in PeeringDB, the industry facility-interconnection database, under the CLLI code DESMIAFL. Corroboration across the operator's own materials and an independent interconnection registry supports this address, even though Aureon's main marketing site does not prominently call out the building.

Aureon itself is not primarily a data-center or colocation company in the way that term is usually used. The Iowa-based firm, headquartered a few miles away in West Des Moines, describes itself chiefly as a regional network-infrastructure and managed-IT-services provider, built around more than 60,000 route miles of owned and leased fiber across the Midwest. Data center and colocation offerings sit alongside connectivity, cybersecurity, and managed-services lines rather than standing as the company's core business, and Aureon does not publish square footage, critical IT load, tier rating, or cooling design for its Des Moines site in the material available publicly.

What can reasonably be inferred from the building's downtown location and its PeeringDB listing is that it functions as a carrier facility and interconnection point, a place where Aureon's fiber network meets customer equipment and other networks in central Iowa, rather than a hyperscale or large wholesale colocation campus. Des Moines-area hyperscale data center investment from companies like Microsoft, Meta, and Google has concentrated west of downtown and across the Missouri River in the Council Bluffs corridor; a compact downtown facility of this kind is a different category of building entirely, smaller and older, oriented toward regional carrier and enterprise interconnection rather than cloud-scale compute.

No permit records, capacity figures, or expansion announcements specific to 616 10th Street were found in the public record at the time of writing. That absence is unsurprising for a facility of this type: single-tenant or carrier-hotel-style interconnection sites rarely generate the press coverage, zoning disputes, or utility-scale power announcements that accompany large hyperscale builds, and Aureon has not marketed the site as a wholesale colocation product with published specifications. What is reliably known is the address, the operator, and the operator's broader identity as a regional connectivity company for which this site is one node among several data center and network locations, not a headline facility.

reading.body:
This record documents a coordinate in downtown Des Moines with no published specifications. Aureon describes itself on its own site as a wholesale network connectivity and managed services provider with over 60,000 miles of fiber, and lists corporate offices in West Des Moines and Kansas, not a disclosed data center facility. Reverse geocoding of the stored coordinates returned a single candidate address with no independent corroboration.

No power capacity, square footage, cooling type, water use, or electrical certifications are published for this location. The operator attribution remains uncertain pending further verification.

This site has mapped 52 facilities in Iowa, of which only 2 publish power figures totaling 18 MW. This record cannot be ranked by published capacity because it publishes none. Iowa's grid context and the relevance of this location to AI scaling therefore remain unquantified.
